newsitem.title: FINLAND: POHJOLA PENSION INSURANCE FCAST UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: POHJOLA PENSION INSURANCE FCAST UNCHANGED.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola Oy said on Thursday its expectations for growth in voluntary pension insurance premium income were unchanged despite uncertainty caused by vague finance ministry plans to cut tax exemptions.
"We have had many concerned phone calls which is completely understandable ... but we think reason will win on this issue," Pohjola life insurance director Jorma Hamalainen told Reuters.
"But we still believe that premium income growth will be 20 to 30 percent this year," he said, adding that last year's pension insurance premium income had been about 400 million markka.
Pohjola's life insurances are sold by associated company mutual Suomi-Salama, but Pohjola plans to take over the operation this year.
Second finance minister Arja Alho has said this week that the 100 percent tax deductability of pension insurance premiums is too generous and that the ministry is planning changes.

Hamalainen said he expected the ministry to step back and at least not cut deductability to 70 percent -- which some media have said it planned -- once it sees the social benefits of voluntary pension schemes.
